attacks.claim: A legal takedown can be undone or left half-done. A queued or retrying `make_responsive_set`, or the backfill, can re-write derivative keys after `purge_image` deletes them. The purge also never clears `has_responsive_set`, so articles (and 60 s cached HTML) keep rendering `<picture>` sources that point at deleted keys. The only purge test covers a finished set.
attacks.evidence: "Test: purge an image with a full responsive set; assert zero remaining keys and one wildcard invalidation." ABSENT: tombstone or deleted-state check in the task and backfill, clearing `has_responsive_set`.

attacks.claim: The claim that wire (AP/Reuters) derivatives are licence-covered rests only on an internal confirmation, with no licence clause cited. Metadata stripping also removes credit and usage-terms fields that wire licences may require preserved, and the plan does not address that. The backfill will publish all of this at scale.
attacks.evidence: "covered by the current licences (photo desk confirmation on WEB-778, Oct 19)." and "all metadata is stripped (`strip=True`)"

attacks.claim: The plan does not say `has_responsive_set` is set only after all 11 derivatives are uploaded. If it is set early, or a retry leaves a partial set, `<source>` URLs can point at missing keys, and browsers do not fall back from a failed `<source>`.
attacks.evidence: "`<picture>` is rendered only when `image.has_responsive_set` is true (set by the task)"

attacks.claim: The success target (CrUX p75 LCP ≤ 2.5 s) is above what the plan's own prototype predicts (2.6 s, in a lab test), and no further lever is named. The rollout is reversible and measured, so this is a risk to the goal rather than a safety issue.
attacks.evidence: "p75 LCP 3.9 s → 2.6 s" vs "CrUX p75 mobile LCP on article pages ≤ 2.5 s within 6 weeks of 100%"

attacks.claim: The JPEG srcset stops at 1200 px, while AVIF and WebP go to 1600 px. The `src` fallback is ignored when srcset is present, so JPEG-only browsers at 2x on a 720 px column get a soft 1200 px image.
attacks.evidence: "JPEG at 480/800/1200 px and AVIF (q 50) and WebP (q 75) at 480/800/1200/1600 px"

attacks.claim: The backfill has about 97% utilisation of the two nights' window (9.7 h of work in 10 h), and the 0.9 s per image figure comes from a small prototype. Running on the same nodes as publishing does not guarantee that publishing is never delayed. The task is idempotent and resumable, so a slip spills into another night rather than failing. Per-task alerting could also flood #web-alerts during a systemic failure.
attacks.evidence: "≈ 9.7 h, run over two nights (01:00–06:00) on a separate low-priority Celery queue, so publishing tasks are never delayed"

attacks.claim: The security argument leans on 'authenticated staff only', but wire and freelancer content and compromised accounts still reach the libvips and libheif decoders. No decode time or memory limits are stated, and the HEIC path is not covered by the metadata test.
attacks.evidence: "Uploads come only from authenticated CMS staff"

attacks.claim: The cost section omits S3 PUT request charges (about 3.4M for the backfill) and cleanup of derivatives from superseded re-crops.
